rationale: The requested experiment executed and completed, and its primary comparison is answered from the retained receipt: a node that recovered through InstallSnapshot keeps a log store index below its snapshot index and then creates fresh snapshots at that same index repeatedly while completely idle. The control comparison could not correlate in that receipt because both observed nodes emitted the same end-event name, so a successor harness (role-specific event names, identical producers and timings) is requested for the control rather than leaving it as an uncorrelated assertion.

limitations: The witness is one bounded window (900ms, SnapshotInterval 40ms, 22 samples) on one recovered node in one cluster; it establishes the condition and the repeated snapshot creation, not production SnapshotInterval cost or how long the condition persists in a busy cluster.

The observation is bounded to the automatic snapshot path on a node isolated from its leader during the window; the receipt does not separate snapshot creations caused by a further InstallSnapshot because isolation excludes that source by construction.

The control comparison in the retained receipt is structurally uncorrelated (both nodes shared one end-event name), so the control is supported by the operands recorded in the same receipt and by the requested successor rather than by a holds outcome.
No safety or availability failure is claimed; the effect is repeated snapshot work, and snapshot retention still bounds how many snapshot objects are kept.

interpretations.rationale: The witnessed conditional execution is the defect: the automatic snapshot condition of a node that recovered through InstallSnapshot is permanently true while the node is idle, so it keeps writing fresh snapshots of unchanged state. Receipt dd59f37872d240548eff168eb821901f (completed, exit 0, tests_passed) parsed five events. Index 0 recovery_state for node server-9f900c62...: the snapshot index advanced from 62 to 202 across the reconnect while the log store last index stayed 62, with log_store_below_snapshot_index true and snapshot_advanced_over_log_store true, i.e. a real InstallSnapshot recovery whose log store was left below the installed snapshot index. Index 1 window_start for that node: should_snapshot true, snapshot index 202, last snapshot index 202, log store last index 62, applied index 202. Index 3 recovered_window_end after 22 samples of 40ms with applied_delta 0: distinct_snapshot_ids 15, snapshot_created_without_new_entries true, newest snapshot index still 202 while the newest ID moved from 2-202-1791708222798 to 2-202-1791708223751, and should_snapshot still true - comparison_index 0 holds with the victim_window admission matched to index 1. The source explains the mechanism: shouldSnapshot (snapshot.go:106-120) compares the log store's LastIndex with the last snapshot index using an unsigned subtraction with no ordering guard, while the snapshot-aware index used elsewhere is max(lastLogIndex, lastSnapshotIndex) (state.go:159-163); installSnapshot (raft.go:1814-1950) sets the last snapshot index to the installed index and compacts with min(snapIdx, lastLogIdx-trailingLogs) (snapshot.go:216-240), so a node whose log store sits below the snapshot keeps that lower index, and runSnapshots (snapshot.go:72-102) calls takeSnapshot every SnapshotInterval while the condition stays true. takeSnapshot succeeds because the FSM-reported index equals the installed snapshot index, which is not below the committed configuration index (snapshot.go:125-211). In the same receipt the control operands are recorded: index 2 and index 4 for the leader, should_snapshot false with a log store index equal to its snapshot index and distinct_snapshot_ids 1 at index 202 over the same window with applied_delta 0; that comparison's outcome in this receipt is unknown only because the shared end-event name prevented correlation, and the successor harness re-requests it with role-specific event names. Consequence and severity: on a node that recovered by snapshot and then stays idle, the node writes a full-state snapshot every SnapshotInterval indefinitely, with the snapshot store reaping older copies - repeated avoidable IO and FSM Snapshot() work rather than a safety or availability violation.

answers.e2a8cfd757e74ee4965e45968de09795-gap-2: Yes, and nothing in the observed path raises the log store index to prevent the repeat. In receipt dd59f37872d240548eff168eb821901f (exit 0) the recovered node's log store last index stayed 62 while its snapshot index was 202 (event index 0, log_store_below_snapshot_index true), shouldSnapshot reported true at window start (index 1) and still true at window end (index 3), and over the 900ms window with applied_delta 0 the node produced 15 distinct snapshot IDs whose newest index remained 202 - so a fresh snapshot at the same index was created roughly every SnapshotInterval. The leader observed in the same window kept shouldSnapshot false with 1 distinct snapshot ID at the same index 202 (indices 2 and 4). The mechanism is the unsigned delta in snapshot.go:106-120 measured against the log store's own LastIndex rather than the snapshot-aware index, combined with installSnapshot setting the snapshot index above the surviving log store index (raft.go:1814-1950, snapshot.go:216-240) and runSnapshots sampling the condition every SnapshotInterval (snapshot.go:72-102).

knowledge.assertion: shouldSnapshot compares the log store's own last index with the snapshot index using an unsigned subtraction with no ordering guard.
a server's reported last index is max(lastLogIndex, lastSnapshotIndex), while installSnapshot updates lastApplied, the last snapshot index and compaction without rewriting the log index.
takeSnapshot only refuses when the FSM-reported index is below the committed configuration index, so the recovered node's snapshot at the installed index is allowed.

counterevidence: The control operands recorded in the same receipt show the condition is not universal: the leader in the same window kept shouldSnapshot false, its log store index equal to its snapshot index, and a single snapshot ID at index 202 with applied_delta 0.

The retained receipt's control comparison outcome is unknown (no correlated prerequisite) because both nodes emitted one shared end-event name; this is a harness naming defect in my comparison setup, not a contrary observation, and it is why a successor is requested rather than treated as confirmation.
The node was isolated during the window by construction, so the repeated snapshots cannot be attributed to further InstallSnapshot traffic from a leader.
limitations: One execution, one bounded window; production SnapshotInterval values, larger state, and busy clusters were not exercised.
The measured effect is repeated snapshot creation on a recovered idle node; no state corruption, lost entry or availability failure is claimed, and snapshot retention bounds stored copies.
The witness does not measure the CPU, IO or FSM Snapshot() latency cost of the repeated snapshots.
Monotonic log stores take the removeOldLogs branch instead of compactLogs and were not exercised.
interpretations.report_title: 快照恢复后自动快照条件恒真导致重复快照
interpretations.report_answer: 已确认的缺陷：经 InstallSnapshot 恢复的节点，其日志存储 LastIndex 可能停留在低于已安装快照索引的位置（installSnapshot 设置快照索引并按 min(snapIdx, lastLogIdx-trailingLogs) 压缩，state.go:159-163 的快照感知索引不参与该判断）。shouldSnapshot（snapshot.go:106-120）用无符号减法比较日志存储索引与快照索引且无大小保护，于是条件恒为真，runSnapshots（snapshot.go:72-102）每个 SnapshotInterval 都会触发一次 takeSnapshot。固定输入执行（receipt dd59f37872d240548eff168eb821901f，exit 0）中：恢复节点快照索引 62→202 而日志存储索引保持 62；在 900ms 窗口、applied_delta 为 0 的情况下产生 15 个不同快照 ID，最新快照索引始终为 202；同一窗口内 leader 的 should_snapshot 为 false 且只有 1 个快照 ID。后果是空闲恢复节点持续写出等价的全量快照（可避免的 IO/快照开销），不主张安全性或可用性被破坏。

experiment.revision_reason: Only the event labelling and comparison wiring changed: the predecessor emitted one shared window_end event for both the recovered node and the leader, so the control comparison could not correlate an admission event to the compared event identity (receipt dd59f37872d240548eff168eb821901f reported comparison_index 1 as unknown with 'No corresponding prerequisite events reached: control_window/window_start'). The successor emits recovered_window_end for the recovered node and control_window_end for the leader with the leader admission renamed control_window_start, keeping the producers, configuration, command counts, isolation steps and window identical. Fresh execution is requested because the comparison basis changed.
experiment.requirement: On a server whose log store last index sits below its last snapshot index, the automatic snapshot condition stays true while the server is idle, and the server's snapshot goroutine keeps creating fresh snapshots at the same index; a server whose log store index equals its snapshot index does not.
experiment.responsibility: shouldSnapshot's delta computation between the log store's LastIndex and the last snapshot index as consumed by runSnapshots, observed on a node recovered through InstallSnapshot and on the leading node of the same cluster as control.

scope.description: One fault-free execution of a normally bootstrapped 3-node in-memory cluster with SnapshotInterval=40ms, SnapshotThreshold=20 and TrailingLogs=5: warm traffic, isolation of one follower, further traffic so the leader compacts, reconnection so the follower recovers by InstallSnapshot, then a bounded idle window on the recovered node (isolated again) with the leader observed over the same window as control. Identical to the predecessor except that the two nodes' window events carry distinct names.
assumptions: MakeCluster(3) with the settings above performs real bootstrap, replication, snapshotting and log compaction through the in-memory transport.
Disconnecting only the chosen follower leaves the leader with a quorum, so the cluster keeps committing and the leader's log compacts past the isolated follower's next index.
Pre-vote is active by default, so the isolated follower does not raise its term and reconnecting lets the leader complete recovery without a spurious election.
Isolating the recovered node again before the window removes the leader as a source of further snapshots, so any new snapshot in that node's store is produced by its own snapshot goroutine.
The leader is idle during the window apart from heartbeats and its log store index equals its snapshot index.
excluded: Safety claims: no state divergence, lost entry or double application is asserted.
Cost measurement: bytes written, disk wear and FSM Snapshot() latency are not measured.
Monotonic log store implementations, which take the removeOldLogs branch instead of compactLogs.
Production SnapshotInterval values and long-run persistence of the condition.

experiment.prefix: Same prefix as the predecessor, built with captured test facilities and real producers only: MakeCluster(3, conf) with SnapshotInterval=40ms, SnapshotThreshold=20, TrailingLogs=5; 60 warm leader.Apply() commands so every node snapshots; c.Disconnect on the chosen follower plus 140 further commands committed by the remaining quorum so the leader compacts past the follower's next index; c.FullyConnect so the follower recovers through the real InstallSnapshot handler; then recovery_state, then c.Disconnect of the recovered node again before the window. The successor differs only in event naming: the recovered node emits window_start and recovered_window_end, the leader emits control_window_start and control_window_end, so each comparison's admission and result events correlate on the same node identity. Window sampling, operands and the derived snapshot_created_without_new_entries field are unchanged from the predecessor. No storage is pre-filled and no production code is modified.

comparisons.description: Recovered node: with no newly applied entries in the window, more than one distinct snapshot ID appears in its own snapshot store, i.e. fresh snapshots are created repeatedly at the same index.
Control: the leader of the same cluster, idle over the same window with its log store index equal to its snapshot index, creates no further snapshots.
